data.gender_notes: Gloria is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'gloria' meaning 'glory, honor, fame'. In Christian tradition, Gloria is a name of praise, signifying the radiant glory of God and the heavenly host. The name Gloria carries the meaning “Glory, Honor, Fame” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Gloria usually hope their child will grow to embody glory, honor, fame and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the radiant, spiritual light that accompanies divine love and grace.
data.etymology: Gloria belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glory, Honor, Fame.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gloria total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gloria has been popular in various cultures and has been used as a given name since ancient times. In the Christian tradition, it gained popularity as a name given to girls to express praise and adoration towards the glory of God and the radiant glory of the angels, as told in the biblical passage, Luke 2:14, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will." Additionally, "Gloria" has been used as the title of several operas, hymns, and musical pieces, reflecting its association with joy, praise, and splendor.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gloria holds deep spiritual significance in the Christian faith. In Catholic and Orthodox traditions, it is associated with the Magnificat, a canticle of Mary, the mother of Jesus, which begins with the words "Gloria in excelsis Deo," translating to "Glory to God in the highest." It also echoes the opening line of the hymn "Gloria," which is sung at Mass and expresses the joyful recognition of the divine majesty and might of God. Through the name Gloria, Christians are reminded of the eternal and infinite glory of God, and are encouraged to offer their praises and thanksgiving in response to His endless love and grace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gloria, meaning "glory" in Latin, symbolizes the radiant and triumphant expression of praise and adoration given to God. It is a reminder of God's glory revealed in the world and in our lives.

The hymn was traditionally sung during the Liturgy of the Hours at night prayer and is still sung in the Roman Rite during the Christmas season.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Gloria has significant roots in Latin American culture and Christianity, making it a popular choice for both Hispanic and Christian communities. It is often used as a given name for babies, and its meaning - 'glory' or 'brightness' - reflects the hope and joy associated with these traditions. In modern times, the name Gloria is seen on various platforms. On social media, it is used as a username, hashtag, or trending topic for content related to Latin American culture, festive occasions, or Christian spirituality. In the music industry, it is the title of popular songs by artists such as Gloria Estefan and Gloria Gaynor. In the fashion industry, it can be found in the names of clothing brands, fashion lines, or even individual garments that evoke a sense of brightness, elegance, or celebratory spirit.
